paragraphs.text: Our boiler has cut out four times since 6 January 2025, and each time the flat is stone cold within two hours. On the morning of 16 January I woke up to 9.8 degrees in my daughter's bedroom while it was minus eight outside, and Bergmann Immobilien AG keeps repeating that the replacement part is on order and nothing can be done until it turns up.

Thermotec Haustechnik came out on 9 January 2025 and wrote the call-up afterwards. From what I remember of their write-up, they blamed a cracked heat exchanger, quoted somewhere around CHF 2,340 for the replacement, and said the part itself was not expected before 20 February. I am going from memory, mind you, since I only read it through once when it came in.

Yesterday evening I went through the folder in my hallway cupboard, and the property manager's run of replies to my defect notice is in there after all, every message in one place. It is sitting on my kitchen table and I can get it over to you whenever you want it. I would rather not paraphrase what is in it and get something wrong.

What I actually need checked is whether I can start paying the rent into a blocked account from 1 March 2025, given that the deadline I set them for 7 February came and went with no repair. What stays unclear to me is whether the delay counts against the landlord at all when the part is genuinely stuck at the supplier; nobody has given me a straight answer on that point.

Before the current decision is taken, the overnight conditions in the occupied rooms must be established from a calibrated temperature or humidity log covering those rooms over the nights in question. A party's account of what such a record shows does not establish its content; the record itself, or an authenticated export of it, has to be on file.

The technical cause of the failure and the contractor's repair plan must likewise be established before this decision. Either the contractor's service report setting out the diagnosis and the planned repair, or an authenticated property-management case export covering diagnosis and response history, is acceptable for this point. A summary or recollection of either record by a party does not establish what it contains; produce the record itself.

Notice of the defect, the repair deadline and the landlord's response history must all be established before the current decision. Acceptable proof is the property manager's response history to the defect notice together with the written repair deadline letter carrying the deposit warning, or in the alternative the authenticated property-management case export covering diagnosis and response history. Here too, what a party says those papers contain does not establish their content; the documents themselves are required.

Medical confirmation of health effects for an occupant is a conditional obligation, not a standing one. It becomes active only once a returned contractor service report on the technical diagnosis and repair plan itself reports health effects on an occupant; until that circumstance appears in the returned report, do not ask the customer for a physician's confirmation.

Photographs of the apartment are not required for this check and should not be requested as part of it. Readiness here means no more than that the listed facts are established from the records required above; it does not settle legal entitlement.

paragraphs.text: Measurement record, Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left, 3000 Bern, drawn up by Klimamess Bern GmbH: readings were taken with a calibrated data logger, serial 41827, calibration certificate of 14 November 2024, valid to 13 November 2025. Values were recorded every fifteen minutes between 22:00 and 07:00 on the nights of 15/16, 16/17 and 18/19 January 2025 and give minima of 11.4 °C in the living room and 9.8 °C in the child's bedroom, with relative humidity between 71 and 78 per cent. Outdoor temperature over the same hours moved between minus 6 °C and minus 8 °C.

Service report, Thermotec Haustechnik GmbH, call-out of 9 January 2025, Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left, 3000 Bern: the Viessmann Vitodens 200 shows a fractured primary heat exchanger with a hairline crack along the lower weld seam, which accounts for the repeated lockouts since 6 January 2025. The unit cannot be returned to service without replacing the exchanger together with the ignition module; both parts were ordered from the supplier on 9 January 2025 at a quoted repair price of CHF 2,340, with delivery indicated for 20 February 2025 at the earliest. During the visit the tenant reported that her seven-year-old daughter has had a persistent cough and broken sleep since the outages began, and the technician recorded that the rooms were cold enough at the time of inspection for the occupants' health to be affected.

Correspondence record, Bergmann Immobilien AG, tenancy Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left, 3000 Bern: the defect notice of 7 January 2025 was acknowledged by e-mail on 8 January 2025, and the heating contractor was instructed the same day. Further replies went to the tenant on 13 January 2025 ('part ordered, no delivery date from the supplier yet'), on 22 January 2025 ('supplier confirms calendar week 8') and on 10 February 2025, which stated that no interim heating would be provided and that the repair would proceed once the part arrived. The tenant's registered letter of 24 January 2025 is recorded as received on 27 January 2025 and was not answered.

Registered letter of 24 January 2025 from Vera Bachmann to Bergmann Immobilien AG: the heating at Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left, has failed repeatedly since 6 January 2025 and remains unrepaired despite the defect notice of 7 January 2025. The landlord is required to restore full heating by 7 February 2025. Should that date pass without repair, the rent from 1 March 2025 onwards will be paid into a blocked account at the Berner Kantonalbank rather than to the landlord, and a reduction will be claimed for the period concerned.

Praxis Dr. med. Sonja Frei, Bern, 19 February 2025: Lena Bachmann, born 12 April 2017, was seen on 21 January and again on 11 February 2025 with a persistent cough and obstructive bronchitis, and inhalation therapy was started at the first consultation. This note sets out the diagnoses and the course of treatment only; the medical assessment of whether the illness is attributable to the cold living conditions is still outstanding, as the practice has not yet received the recorded room temperatures. A completed confirmation including that assessment will follow once those figures are to hand.

Praxis Dr. med. Sonja Frei, Bern, 3 March 2025: Lena Bachmann, born 12 April 2017, was treated on 21 January and 11 February 2025 for obstructive bronchitis with a persistent nocturnal cough; no comparable episode appears anywhere in her history before January 2025. Having now reviewed the overnight room readings of 9.8 °C to 11.4 °C recorded in the flat over the same weeks, I confirm from a medical standpoint that prolonged exposure to those indoor temperatures is the probable cause of the episodes, and that no lasting recovery is to be expected while the rooms remain unheated.

Authenticated case export, Bergmann Immobilien AG, file 2025-0114, generated on 26 February 2025 and signed with the company's qualified electronic seal: the export reproduces the technical diagnosis entered on 9 January 2025 for the tenancy at Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left — fractured primary heat exchanger, exchanger and ignition module ordered, repair price CHF 2,340, supplier delivery indicated for 20 February 2025. The correspondence history with the tenant is not carried in this export, because the message archive for January and February 2025 was still being migrated when the file was generated. The missing section covering that correspondence will be exported and transmitted as soon as the migration is finished.

Authenticated case export, Bergmann Immobilien AG, file 2025-0114, generated on 14 March 2025 under the company's qualified electronic seal: the technical entry of 9 January 2025 records a fractured primary heat exchanger on the Viessmann Vitodens 200 at Lindenstrasse 12, third floor left, with the exchanger and the ignition module ordered the same day at a repair price of CHF 2,340 and supplier delivery indicated for 20 February 2025. The correspondence section logs the defect notice received on 7 January 2025, its acknowledgement on 8 January 2025, status replies on 13 and 22 January 2025, receipt on 27 January 2025 of the tenant's registered letter of 24 January 2025 setting 7 February 2025 for completion, and the reply of 10 February 2025 declining interim heating. At the date of this export the repair was still open.

Image set from the tenant's phone, twelve frames all dated 3 August 2024: the balcony in full afternoon sun with tomato plants in terracotta pots, a close-up of the newly tiled splashback in the bathroom, and several shots of the hallway after the walls were repainted in pale green. Two further frames show the neighbour's cat asleep on the windowsill, and the last one is of a birthday cake with candles on the kitchen table.

paragraphs.text: Our boiler at Lindenweg 14 in Köniz has cut out three times since the turn of the year: first on the evening of 8 January 2025, then again on 14 and on 21 January, each time during the hardest frost. On the morning of 22 January there was ice on the inside of the living-room window frames, and since then we have been keeping two rooms going with borrowed electric radiators. Wyss Haustechnik told me on 16 January 2025 that the replacement ignition control unit had been ordered, yet nothing has been fitted to this day.

Going through the folder in the hallway cupboard yesterday, I came across the service report that Wyss Haustechnik drew up after their January visits, and I have it here in front of me. I would rather not paraphrase what the technician put in it; just tell me where to send it and it goes out the same day.

As I recall it, the measurement service set the logger to record the bedroom as well as the living room, and I am fairly certain it ran over three separate nights in January 2025. Brunner Immobilien AG maintain that only one single night in the hallway was ever recorded and that nothing at all was measured in the rooms we actually sleep in. Both accounts cannot be true, and after six weeks I no longer trust my own memory of what the printout showed.

What I need looked at now is whether we may deposit the rent from the March 2025 payment onwards and claim a reduction for the weeks since 8 January. What I genuinely cannot work out is who carries the delay: Brunner Immobilien AG point to the supplier of the ordered component, while Wyss Haustechnik say the order only left their desk once the management had approved the quote.

Medical confirmation, Dr. med. Andrea Keller, general practice, Schwarzenburgstrasse 12, Köniz, issued 6 February 2025. Mrs Irene Bucher, born 3 April 1949, resident at Lindenweg 14, 3rd floor, consulted me on 24 January and again on 3 February 2025 with acute bronchitis and markedly raised blood pressure. In my assessment both conditions were aggravated by her prolonged exposure to night-time room temperatures of about 11 °C in the flat; antibiotic treatment was prescribed on 24 January 2025 and I advised her to stay elsewhere until the heating has been restored.

Living room, night of 14-15 January 2025: lowest value 11.4 °C; night of 20-21 January 2025: lowest value 10.9 °C. The bedroom channel could not be read out of the device before this record was issued, so no bedroom readings appear here; the complete record covering both rooms follows once the device has been exported again.

Measurement record, Lindenweg 14, 3rd floor, Köniz — logger MK-220, calibrated 3 December 2024 under certificate 220-4471, readings taken every ten minutes from 22:00 to 07:00. Living room: lowest values of 11.4 °C on the night of 14-15 January 2025, 10.9 °C on 20-21 January 2025 and 11.2 °C on 27-28 January 2025; bedroom: 10.8 °C, 10.3 °C and 10.6 °C on the same three nights, with relative humidity between 71 and 78 per cent throughout. Both rooms are in daily use by the household as living room and sleeping room respectively.

Cover note, Wyss Haustechnik GmbH, 3 February 2025, job 2025-0418. The copy of our service report that went out with this message came off the scanner badly: pages 2 and 3 are missing altogether and the one remaining page is too dark to be read. We can therefore confirm nothing from it at this stage, and a clean copy will be produced once the original is back from our Bern office.

Service report, Wyss Haustechnik GmbH, job 2025-0418, site Lindenweg 14, 3rd floor, Köniz; drawn up 24 January 2025 by technician Thomas Lüthi after the visits of 13, 16 and 22 January 2025. Diagnosis: the ignition control unit of the Vitola 200 gas boiler, installed in 2009, is intermittently faulty and shuts the burner down under sustained load, which accounts for the outages of 8, 14 and 21 January 2025; the expansion vessel has additionally reached the end of its service life and holds no pre-charge pressure. Repair plan: fitting of the replacement ignition control unit ordered on 16 January 2025, renewal of the expansion vessel and a subsequent pressure test, to be carried out on the first working day after delivery, quoted at CHF 2,340 including labour.

Response history, Brunner Immobilien AG, file 44-LW14, tenancy Bucher, Lindenweg 14, 3rd floor. The tenant's written defect notice of 9 January 2025 reached us on 10 January 2025 and was acknowledged by e-mail the same day; Wyss Haustechnik GmbH was instructed on 11 January and attended the property on 13 January 2025, and the spare part was reported to us as ordered on 16 January 2025, of which the tenant was informed on 24 January and again on 7 February 2025. The tenant's deadline letter of 22 January 2025 was received on 23 January 2025 and remained unanswered in writing on our side until 11 February 2025, when we confirmed the repair date of 19 February 2025.

Köniz, 22 January 2025. To Brunner Immobilien AG, regarding the heating defect at Lindenweg 14, 3rd floor: the gas boiler failed on 8, 14 and 21 January 2025 and the flat has not been properly heatable since, with room temperatures around 11 °C at night. I hereby set you a deadline until 5 February 2025 to have the defect repaired. Should the repair not be completed by that date, I will deposit the rent of CHF 1,680 per month with the depository office of the Canton of Bern from the March 2025 payment onwards, until the defect has been remedied. Daniel Bucher.

Six photographs from the tenant's phone, all carrying the date 21 June 2024: the balcony after the railing had been repainted, two views of the freshly planted herb boxes on the parapet, and a birthday lunch with seven guests around the garden table. The remaining two frames show the bicycle shed at the rear of the building and a cat asleep on the doormat of the neighbouring flat.

paragraphs.text: Seit dem 8. Januar 2025 fällt die Heizung in unserer Wohnung am Lindenweg 14 immer wieder aus, am schlimmsten in der Nacht auf den 15. Januar, als es draussen minus neun Grad hatte und wir morgens in Jacken in der Küche sassen. Der Kessel läuft jeweils ein paar Stunden und schaltet dann auf Störung; seit dem 22. Januar heisst es, ein Ersatzteil sei bestellt und man warte auf die Lieferung.

Frau Keller von der Hausverwaltung Lehmann AG hat mich am 27. Januar 2025 angerufen und mir am Telefon durchgegeben, was in meinem Fristschreiben vom 20. Januar festgehalten ist: Termin 31. Januar 2025 und die Ankündigung, die Mietzinse danach zu hinterlegen. Ich gebe das hier nur so wieder, wie sie es mir geschildert hat, denn im Wortlaut vor mir hatte ich das Schreiben in diesem Gespräch nicht.

Das Schreiben, von dem ich Ihnen erzählt habe, liegt bei mir zu Hause im Ordner; darin ist festgehalten, wie auf meine Meldung vom 9. Januar reagiert wurde und welche Termine dabei genannt worden sind. Ich suche es heraus, wenn Sie es brauchen.

Bitte prüfen Sie, ob mein Fall jetzt weiterbearbeitet werden kann — es geht um die Mietzinsreduktion und um die Stromkosten der beiden Elektroöfen, die wir seit Mitte Januar laufen lassen. Unklar ist mir dabei vor allem, welche Unterlagen Sie wirklich von mir brauchen und ob das, was mir die Verwaltung am Telefon gesagt hat, für Sie überhaupt zählt.

paragraphs.text: Messtechnik Wyss AG, Auswertung zur Wohnung Lindenweg 14, 3. Stock, Burgdorf: Für den Zeitraum vom 14. bis 23. Januar 2025 liegen die Werte aus Wohnzimmer und Schlafzimmer bis jeweils 22:00 Uhr vor. Die Aufzeichnungen zwischen 22:00 und 06:00 Uhr sind in dieser Auswertung nicht enthalten, weil der Export aus dem Logger abgebrochen wurde; die Nachtwerte liefern wir nach, sobald der Datensatz erneut ausgelesen ist.

Messprotokoll Lindenweg 14, 3. Stock, Burgdorf — Logger Testo 175 H1, Kalibrierschein Nr. 2024-1187 vom 4. November 2024, Aufzeichnung im 15-Minuten-Takt in Wohnzimmer und Schlafzimmer. In der Nacht vom 14. auf den 15. Januar 2025 sank die Temperatur im Schlafzimmer von 15,2 °C um 22:00 Uhr auf 11,8 °C um 05:15 Uhr, im Wohnzimmer bis auf 12,6 °C. In der Nacht vom 22. auf den 23. Januar 2025 lagen die Tiefstwerte bei 12,1 °C im Schlafzimmer und 13,0 °C im Wohnzimmer, die relative Feuchte durchgehend zwischen 68 und 72 Prozent.

Wärmetechnik Roth GmbH, Servicerapport vom 24. Januar 2025 zum Einsatz vom 23. Januar 2025, Objekt Lindenweg 14, Öl-Heizkessel Baujahr 2009: Der Feuerungsautomat meldete beim Test den Fehlercode 128 und verriegelte nach drei bis fünf Betriebsstunden auf Störung. Als Ursache haben wir die defekte Steuerplatine des Feuerungsautomaten festgestellt; ein Ersatz derselben Bauart wurde am 24. Januar 2025 beim Lieferanten bestellt, Liefertermin 5. Februar 2025, Einbau und Inbetriebnahme vorgesehen auf den 6. Februar 2025. Bis dahin läuft die Wohnung im Notbetrieb mit zwei mobilen Elektroheizern.

Januar 2025 haben wir sie bestätigt und den Servicetechniker angekündigt, der am 16. Januar 2025 vor Ort war. Ihr Schreiben mit der Fristansetzung auf den 31. Januar 2025 erreichte uns am 21. Januar 2025; am 24. Januar 2025 haben wir Ihnen die Bestellung des Ersatzteils mitgeteilt und am 30. Januar 2025 den 6. Februar 2025 als Reparaturtermin genannt.

Burgdorf, 20. Januar 2025, an die Hausverwaltung Lehmann AG: Hiermit setze ich Ihnen Frist bis zum 31. Januar 2025, um die Heizung in der Wohnung Lindenweg 14, 3. Stock, wieder dauerhaft in Betrieb zu nehmen. Bleibt der Mangel über diesen Termin hinaus bestehen, werde ich den monatlichen Mietzins von CHF 1'480.— ab dem 1. Februar 2025 bei der kantonalen Hinterlegungsstelle hinterlegen, bis die Heizung wieder einwandfrei läuft.

Hausarztpraxis am Marktplatz, Dr. med. Sandra Baumann, Burgdorf, 10. Februar 2025: Für die Bewohnerinnen und Bewohner der Wohnung Lindenweg 14, 3. Stock, wurde in dieser Praxis zu keinem Zeitpunkt eine ärztliche Bestätigung über gesundheitliche Folgen der Heizsituation ausgestellt. Eine solche Bescheinigung existiert nicht und kann deshalb auch nicht herausgegeben werden.

Januar 2025, unsere Bestätigung vom 13. Januar 2025, der Technikereinsatz vom 16. Januar 2025, der Eingang der Fristansetzung auf den 31. Januar 2025 am 21. März 2025, und nachdem die von mir gesetzte Frist am 18. April 2025 ergebnislos verstrichen war, stand am Morgen des 22. April 2025 erneut Wasser im Schrank. Seither bleibt die Küche dauernd feucht, und die angrenzenden Zimmer riechen muffig.

Am 15. Mai 2025 hat mir Frau Küng von der Brunner Immobilien AG am Telefon erzählt, eine Messfirma habe über zwei Nächte kalibrierte Werte zu Temperatur und Luftfeuchtigkeit im Wohn- und im Schlafzimmer aufgezeichnet, und die Feuchtigkeit sei dabei deutlich zu hoch ausgefallen. Bei der Brunner Immobilien AG wird zu jeder Mängelmeldung festgehalten, wann und wie darauf reagiert wurde; zu unserem Fall besteht eine solche Aufstellung ebenfalls. Was darin im Einzelnen steht, entzieht sich meiner Kenntnis, und bei uns zu Hause liegt sie jedenfalls nicht.

What I would like looked at now is whether the leak counts as the landlord's responsibility and whether the damage to the cabinet and the floor underneath is covered. What I still cannot work out is who is supposed to produce the paperwork that is missing, the management, the plumbing firm, or me.

paragraphs.text: Messprotokoll Raumklima, Wohnung Lindenstrasse 14, 3007 Bern, Schlafzimmer: Datenlogger Testo 174H, Nr. 41-2207, kalibriert am 4. Der Instandstellungsplan mit den vorgesehenen Massnahmen, dem Materialbedarf und dem Ausführungstermin fehlt in dieser Fassung, weil die Offerte für Ventil und Strangspülung noch beim Lieferanten liegt. Januar 2025, Antwort der Verwaltung am 23. Januar 2025 mit Verweis auf das Lüftungsverhalten, Aktennotiz zum Befund des Heizungsmonteurs am 7. März 2025 teilten wir der Mieterschaft mit, zuerst eine eigene Begehung abwarten zu wollen; bis zum Ablauf der gesetzten Frist am 14. März 2025 wurde weder eine Reparatur ausgeführt noch ein Termin dafür bestätigt, die Begehung erfolgte am 26. März 2025.

April 2025 zu CHF 2'380 vorgemerkt. Die Übereinstimmung dieses Auszugs mit dem Originaldossier wird hiermit bestätigt.

Mai 2025 aus der Wohnung an der Lindenstrasse 14: der neu bepflanzte Balkonkasten mit Tomaten und Basilikum, der in Salbeigrün gestrichene Küchenschrank, die Katze auf dem Sofa sowie zwei Aufnahmen der Gäste am Geburtstagsessen im Wohnzimmer. My partner and I have been sleeping in the living room since 26 January 2025.

Raumklima Kontrolle GmbH ran calibrated loggers in our bedroom and living room for two weeks in February, and their technician, Herr Amrein, told me on 4 March 2025 that the readout goes out to you automatically as soon as it has been countersigned, so I do not have to request anything. He expects it to reach you within the next few days.

One point about the deadline letter I sent to the property management needs flagging: the version I wrote on 3 March 2025 still carried the numbers from an outdated rent statement, CHF 1,480 net rent and a deadline of 17 March. I spotted the mistake the same week and issued a corrected letter on 7 March 2025 with the actual net rent of CHF 1,740 and the deadline of 24 March 2025, so the earlier figures no longer apply.

What I would like checked now is whether the cold bedroom radiator and the damp wall are being handled as one single defect, and whether my decision to deposit the rent from April onwards is on safe ground. What I genuinely cannot judge is whose account of the cause carries weight here; the management points at our airing habits, I point at the heating, and I have no idea what it would take to settle that between us.

Februar 2025 waren Termine mit der Heizungsbau Brunner GmbH abgemacht, ich habe beide Male zu Hause gewartet, und hinterher hiess es bei der Rüegg & Partner AG, man habe keinen Zutritt zur Wohnung erhalten.

Ende Januar liess ich von einer Messfirma ein geeichtes Gerät im Schlafzimmer aufstellen; besonders in Erinnerung ist mir die Nacht auf den 7. Februar 2025, als die Temperatur gegen 05:20 Uhr auf gut 15 Grad sank und die Luftfeuchtigkeit fast 80 Prozent erreichte. Mai 2025 zu Gesicht bekam, führte nur einen einzigen Zutrittstermin auf, nannte als Datum der ersten Antwort den 5. Februar und wies einen zu tiefen Mietzins aus. Mir geht es jetzt um die Frage, ob der Mietzins für die Monate mit der kalten, feuchten Wohnung herabgesetzt wird und wer die Kosten der Messung trägt. Unklar bleibt mir vor allem, ob mir die beiden Termine angelastet werden, an denen ich nachweislich zu Hause war, und ab welchem Datum die Verwaltung überhaupt als säumig gilt.

I ran a logger in the bedroom and the living room for a week at the start of February 2025, and the first set of night-time readings I passed on was simply wrong, because the device had been put in place before it was calibrated and the figures came out several degrees too warm. Klimadat GmbH re-issued the readings for 3 to 10 February 2025 with the corrected values a few days later. The earlier numbers should be disregarded.

What I would like looked at now is whether the file is at the point where the cold rooms and the damp wall can be handled together as one defect, or whether something is still missing from our side. Honestly, I cannot tell what the disputed access on 22 January and 5 February 2025 does to our position, nor whether the deadline letter I wrote at the end of February 2025 still counts for anything now that 10 March 2025 has passed without any repair.

paragraphs.text: Since 14 January 2025 the radiators in our flat at Lindenweg 14 have stayed lukewarm, and dark damp patches keep spreading along the outer wall of the bedroom; on 20 January I wiped standing water off the window reveal twice in one day. Two service appointments were arranged with Fehr Haustechnik, one on 23 January and one on 4 February 2025, and neither of them ended in an inspection: the firm's office insists that nobody opened the door, while my wife and I sat at home through both time slots. The result is that the dampness has to this day never actually been looked at by anyone from the building side.

Karin Brunner of Brunner Immobilien rang me on 3 April 2025 and said her office can pull a signed case export straight out of their management system, one that covers the technical diagnosis as well as the whole record of how they reacted from the January notice onwards. I have never laid eyes on that export myself; I am only passing on what she told me over the telephone.

Clearing out the hall cupboard yesterday I came across the service report that Fehr Haustechnik left with us after their March visit. It is here at home in paper form and I can send it over the moment you want it. I would rather not paraphrase what the technician wrote in it, since I am no heating engineer.

On the overnight measurements my memory and the management's account do not agree. I am fairly certain that the people from Klimalog placed loggers in the bedroom as well as the living room during the week of 18 February 2025, because I remember shifting a chair to make room for the second unit; Ms Brunner maintains that the service only ever recorded the living room and that nothing was ever run in the bedroom. One of us is misremembering, and from where I sit I cannot tell which.

What I would like looked into now is whether the cold radiators and the damp walls go back to one and the same heating defect, and whether the way my notice was handled puts me in a position to withhold or deposit the rent. What stays genuinely unclear to me is which of those two points you are already in a position to settle, and what you still need from the management or from the heating firm before you can.

paragraphs.text: I was a month behind with the rent of CHF 1,840.00 for my flat at Rosenweg 14 in Olten, and on 2 May 2025 I transferred the whole amount to Brunner Verwaltung AG. The termination letter from Hartmann Immobilien AG is dated 12 May 2025, so the money had left my account ten days before that. When I telephoned the manager, Mr Brunner told me the payment only turned up on the rent account on 14 May 2025 and that in his books it therefore arrived after the termination had gone out.

From what I remember of the official form we were given, it names 30 June 2025 as the day the tenancy ends and puts the outstanding rent at CHF 1,840.00. I read it through twice that evening, and there was no word anywhere in it about the transfer I had already made.

Then there is that letter setting out, step by step, when each notice went out and when it was supposedly handed over. A colleague glanced at it and said the dates in it did not sit well with what the manager had told me on the telephone, although I honestly could not say whether it is the same paper the manager waved at me in the stairwell or a different one altogether.

On 16 May 2025 I rang my bank, and the adviser at Valiant, Ms Keller, looked the transfer up while I was still on the line. She said the order had been carried out on 2 May 2025 and that it carried the same value date, and that the export from their system would show precisely that. I am only repeating what she told me over the telephone; I have not seen that record with my own eyes.

What I would like looked at now is whether a termination can stand when the rent had already left my account before the notice was written. What I still cannot make sense of is why the manager's books speak of 14 May 2025 while my bank speaks of 2 May 2025, and which of those two dates is the one that counts.

This is shown by the property-manager ledger recording the posting and the allocation of the payment. A description or recollection of that ledger, whether given in writing or on the telephone, does not establish what it says; the ledger itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

The content of the cure notice and of the termination notice, and the service of both, must be established before the current decision. Either route is acceptable: the cure notice bearing the termination warning as it was served, together with the termination notice on the official form and the registered-mail or delivery proof for those notices; or the authenticated chronology packet from the landlord's system covering the notices and their service. No party's account of what a notice said or when it arrived carries this point; the documents themselves, or the authenticated export, are required.

paragraphs.text: I was a month behind with the April rent, I admit that, but the money left my account on 6 May 2025 and Seeblick Immobilien AG only wrote the termination afterwards. When I rang Keller Verwaltungs AG on 20 May 2025, the woman on the phone told me their books show the amount arriving on 19 May, which is after the notice had already gone out.

I called Valiant Bank on Monday morning about the transfer. They told me they produce the payment record for this kind of case themselves and will send it across within the next few days, so there is nothing I need to order or chase.
The letter is still here at home, in the folder with everything the post office handed me. If the document is of any use to you, tell me where to send it and it goes out the same day.

What I would like looked at is whether a termination can stand when the rent had already gone out of my account before the notice was written. What I cannot work out on my own is why the payment sits in their books on 19 May when my bank has it leaving on 6 May, and which of those two dates is the one that actually counts.

Before the present question is decided, the execution date and the value date of the rent payment must be established as attested by the bank. The acceptable evidence is the bank's own export of the transfer showing both dates; what a party recalls or describes about such a record does not establish its content, so the record itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

It must also be established, before the present decision, how the property manager booked the payment on its own side, meaning the posting date and the claim the amount was allocated to. This is shown by the manager's ledger for the tenant account covering that posting and allocation; a party's description or recollection of that ledger does not establish what it contains, and the ledger itself or an authenticated export of it must be obtained.

The content and the service of the demand letter carrying the termination warning and of the termination notice must likewise be established before the present decision. Either route is acceptable: the demand letter in the form served, together with the termination notice on the official form and the postal service's delivery proof for those notices, or instead the authenticated chronology packet exported from the landlord's system covering the notices and their service. An account given by a party of what these documents say does not establish their content; the documents themselves, or the authenticated export, are required.

One obligation is conditional: a separate allocation statement becomes necessary only where the sum demanded turns out to have covered more than the rent alone. That condition is triggered by the property manager's ledger once it comes back and reports such a mixed demand, and until the ledger reports it, the allocation statement is not to be requested.

The signed lease contract plays no part in this check and does not need to be called in. Readiness means no more than that the listed facts are established from the documents required for them; it decides nothing about legal entitlement or about the validity of the termination.

Official form for the notice of termination of a residential lease, issued by Seeblick Immobilien AG on 14 May 2025 in respect of the apartment at Hardstrasse 42, 8400 Winterthur, tenant Marc Brunner. The lease is terminated under Art. 257d CO with effect from 30 June 2025, on the ground that no payment of the April 2025 rent of CHF 1,840.00 was recorded within the thirty-day period set by the letter of 9 April 2025. The form names the conciliation authority of the district of Winterthur and the thirty-day period from receipt within which the termination may be challenged.

paragraphs.text: Am 27. März 2025 habe ich den Mietzins für die Wohnung an der Lindenstrasse 14 in Bern überwiesen, also deutlich vor Ablauf der Frist, welche mir die Verwaltung gesetzt hatte. Offen geblieben ist einzig die Rechnung über CHF 420.00 für den Ersatz des Kühlschranks, weil ich bis heute nicht einsehe, dass ich dafür aufkommen muss. Auf dem Kontoblatt der Verwaltung erscheint nun aber nur ein einziger Gesamtbetrag, sodass es aussieht, als hätte ich überhaupt nichts bezahlt.

Das Mahnschreiben mit der Kündigungsandrohung datiert, soweit ich mich erinnere, vom 5. März 2025; darin stand, ich hätte CHF 2'080.00 innert dreissig Tagen zu begleichen. Den genauen Wortlaut habe ich nicht mehr im Kopf, die Summe ist mir aber geblieben, weil sie eben nicht nur den Mietzins umfasste.

Frau Brunner von der Verwaltung hat mir am Telefon erwähnt, dass die Vermieterin ihre Schreiben und deren Versand in einem eigenen System führt und daraus ein beglaubigter Auszug gezogen werden kann. Was dort im Einzelnen verzeichnet ist, weiss ich nicht, und bei mir zu Hause liegt davon nichts.

Bitte prüfen Sie, ob die Kündigung überhaupt standhält, wenn der Mietzins rechtzeitig auf dem Konto der Verwaltung eingetroffen ist. Unklar bleibt für mich vor allem, wie sich der geforderte Gesamtbetrag zusammensetzt und ob meine Zahlung tatsächlich dem Mietzins gutgeschrieben wurde.

paragraphs.text: I transferred the March rent of CHF 1,840.00 to Rüegg Immobilien AG on 27 March 2025, comfortably inside the period the management had set me, and my e-banking shows the money leaving my account the following day. What I did not pay was the CHF 312.50 they billed me on 11 February 2025 for the fridge repair, since I still believe that one is the landlady's to carry. On the statement that reached me afterwards, though, the two were pulled together into a single outstanding figure of CHF 2,152.50, which is what makes the whole thing look unpaid.

Yesterday evening I worked through the box of post I keep in the hallway cupboard, and the delivery slips for both registered letters from the management turned up. They are lying here at home in front of me. I would rather not paraphrase what is printed on them, but I can drop them in the post or scan them over to you today.

About the termination itself, my memory is that what came through the letterbox on 10 April 2025 was an ordinary letter on the management's own paper, with nothing on it that looked like the official cantonal form. Frau Brunner's office tells me the opposite, namely that the notice went out on 9 April 2025 on the proper form, duly signed, ending the lease as of 31 May 2025. One of us has this wrong and I cannot tell which.

What I would like looked at is whether the termination can stand at all, given that the rent itself was in their account inside the period they set me. The part I cannot work out on my own is whether the unpaid repair bill may be rolled into that same demand and held against me, or whether it has to be kept apart from the rent question altogether.

paragraphs.text: On 28 March 2025 I sent the rent of CHF 1,890 for February to Brunner & Partner Immobilien AG, and my bank shows the money leaving my account with a value date of 31 March 2025, well inside the deadline I had been given. The CHF 640 the landlord wants for the replacement fridge I did not pay, because I consider that charge to be his and not mine. What worries me is that the manager's account statement carries only one open figure of CHF 2,530 for the whole tenancy, so there is nothing in it to show that the rent as such was settled in time.

When I rang the landlord's office at Kaufmann Immobilien AG on 14 April 2025, the woman there said the termination on the official form goes out to the tenant automatically in these cases, so there is nothing for me to request. She reckoned it would be in my letterbox within a few days.

There is also that letter out of the landlord's system, the one that lists everything the office sent me and on which day. My sister read it when she helped me go through the post, and now I honestly could not say whether it was the same paper that came in the registered envelope or a separate one.

What I want checked is whether the termination holds up at all, given that the rent was with the manager before the deadline of 4 April 2025 had run out. Where I am completely at sea is the fridge invoice: I do not understand whether an amount like that counts towards the same deadline as the rent, or whether it belongs on a different footing altogether.

Before the present decision is taken, the execution date and the value date of the payment must stand established as attested by the bank. The acceptable source is the bank's own export of the rent payment carrying both of those dates. An account given by a party of what a record says does not establish its content; the record itself, or an authenticated export of it, has to be obtained.

Establish, ahead of the decision, how the payment was posted on the manager's side and against which claim it was set off. The acceptable source is the property manager's ledger recording the posting and the allocation of that payment. A description or recollection offered by a party about what such a ledger contains does not establish its content; work from the ledger itself or from an authenticated export.

The content of the cure notice bearing the termination warning and of the termination notice, together with the manner in which each was served, must be established before the decision is reached. Acceptable are either the served cure notice with the termination warning, the termination notice on the official form and the postal delivery proof taken together, or the authenticated chronology packet drawn from the landlord's system covering the notices and their service. What a party reports a notice to have said does not establish it; the documents themselves, or the authenticated export, are needed.

A separate allocation statement for a demand that mixes rent with other items comes into play only where a returned property-manager ledger reports that such a mixed demand exists. Until a returned ledger reports that circumstance, this obligation stays inactive, and the property manager's ledger is not to be requested on its account.

The signed lease contract is not among the items needed for this check. Readiness means that the listed facts stand established on the strength of the documents called for; it does not settle the legal entitlement of either side.

paragraphs.text: Seit dem 1. April 2022 miete ich die 2.5-Zimmer-Wohnung an der Weissensteinstrasse 41 in 3007 Bern. Weil ich von Februar bis August 2025 beruflich in Lausanne eingesetzt war, meldete ich der Verwaltung Sennhauser & Co. AG am 21. Januar 2025 schriftlich meine dortige Korrespondenzadresse; die Mahnung mit Kündigungsandrohung vom 12. Mai 2025 ging trotzdem an die alte Berner Adresse und erreichte mich nie. Die Kündigung dagegen fand ich am 12. Juli 2025 bei einem Wochenendbesuch im Briefkasten, ganz gewöhnlich mit der B-Post zugestellt, ohne Einschreiben und ohne Abholungseinladung.

Die Verwaltung Sennhauser & Co. AG hat mir am Telefon zugesichert, dass sie mir den Auszug aus ihrer Mieterbuchhaltung mit der Verbuchung und der Anrechnung meiner Zahlung von sich aus zustellt; ich muss dafür nichts weiter unternehmen. Von wenigen Tagen war die Rede, spätestens bis Ende der kommenden Woche soll das Schreiben bei mir sein.

Das amtliche Kündigungsformular habe ich gestern Abend zu Hause in meiner Ablage wiedergefunden, es liegt bei mir im Ordner zur Wohnung. Was genau darauf vermerkt ist, gebe ich hier nicht wieder, aber ich kann Ihnen das Formular jederzeit zukommen lassen.

Soweit ich weiss, führt die Vermieterin in ihrem eigenen System ein beglaubigtes Auszugspaket zu den Schreiben und deren Versand, und die Verwaltung hat darauf Zugriff. Bei mir liegt so etwas nicht, und ich kann auch nichts darüber sagen, was dort festgehalten ist.

Bitte prüfen Sie für mich, ob die Kündigung vom 26. Juni 2025 überhaupt gültig zustande gekommen ist, nachdem der Mietzins für Mai 2025 bereits am 5. Mai 2025 ab meinem Konto ausgeführt wurde. Unklar bleibt mir vor allem, ob es rechtlich eine Rolle spielt, dass die Mahnung an eine Adresse ging, an der ich damals nachweislich nicht erreichbar war.

paragraphs.text: Since 9 January 2025 the post for this tenancy should have been going to the temporary address I gave Keller Immobilien Treuhand in writing while I am working in Lausanne. Instead, the letter setting me a deadline to settle the arrears was dated 6 February 2025 and went to Rosenweg 14, where nobody was picking up the mail, so I heard nothing about it for weeks. The termination itself simply lay in the Rosenweg letterbox as an ordinary item of post; my brother found it there on 26 March 2025 and phoned me the same evening.

On 27 March 2025 I got Frau Keller of the management office on the telephone and asked her what exactly had been issued. She told me it was done on the official cantonal form, signed for Hofgut Immobilien AG, dated 21 March 2025 and naming 30 April 2025 as the end of the lease. All of that is simply what she said to me over the line; I have never had that form in front of me.

There is also the letter my brother put aside for me, the one carrying a post office stamp and a long number across the top. I would like that document looked at properly, because I cannot tell from it who received anything, or on which day.

Frau Keller insists that the management's own system log records my change of address from 9 January 2025 and shows both the reminder and the termination going out to Lausanne. My recollection is quite different: when I rang the office on 14 February 2025, the woman I spoke to read the Rosenweg address back to me as the only one on file and made no mention of Lausanne at all.

What I would like established now is whether the termination can hold at all, given that the deadline letter went to an address I had already asked them to stop using, and whether my transfer of 18 February 2025 arrived in time. What I genuinely cannot work out is why CHF 270.00 is still shown as open against the January rent after I paid CHF 1,780.00, and whether that money was booked against the rent at all or against something else entirely.

Before the present decision is reached, the execution date and the value date of the rent payment must be established as attested by the bank. The acceptable source is the bank's own export of the payment, showing when the order was executed and which value date was applied to it. A party's account or recollection of what such a record says does not establish its content; the record itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

It must also be established beforehand how the payment was posted on the manager's side and to which items it was applied. The acceptable source is the property manager's ledger for this tenancy showing that posting together with the allocation of the sum received. A description given by a party, however detailed, does not establish what the ledger says; the ledger itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

The content and the service of both the cure notice and the termination must be established before the decision is taken. This may rest either on the cure notice with its termination warning as served, together with the termination on the official form and the postal proof of registered dispatch or delivery of those notices, or else on the authenticated chronology packet drawn from the landlord's system covering the notices and their service. What a party reports about the wording or the sending of these notices does not establish it; the documents themselves, or the authenticated export, are required.

An allocation statement for a mixed demand is a conditional obligation: it arises only where the property manager's ledger, once it comes back, reports that the amount called in combined the rent with further items. Until such a report is on file the obligation stays dormant, and that statement is not to be requested.

The signed lease contract is not among the documents needed for this check and should not be pursued for it. Readiness here means only that the listed facts stand established on the documents required for them; it is not a ruling on legal entitlement.

paragraphs.text: Andrea and I have rented the flat at Lindenweg 14 in Wetzikon together since 2019, and it is the home we share with our two children. On 15 April 2025 the postman had me sign for a registered letter from Hauser Immobilien AG, and that is how we learned the tenancy had been given notice as of 31 May 2025. The envelope carried my name alone, and Andrea, who signed the lease together with me, was never addressed in her own name at all.

The notice was issued on the official cantonal form. That form sits in the tenancy file at Hauser Immobilien AG, and the owner, Mr Jürg Rütimann, is said to keep a copy of it as well; I would rather not put words in anyone's mouth about what stands on it.

What I would like looked at is whether a notice directed to me alone can take effect when the flat is our family home and Andrea is a tenant under the same lease. It is also unclear to me whether anything was genuinely still open on the day the notice was written, because I transferred the amount the manager had called in on 28 March 2025. Whether the deadline from the March letter had already run out by then is something I simply cannot judge.

paragraphs.text: My wife Petra and I have rented the flat at Lindenweg 12 in Wetzikon as our family home since 2016, and on 12 April 2025 I signed at the door for a registered letter from Hofmatt Immobilien AG that was made out to me alone. It was a termination of our lease; Petra's name appears nowhere on it and nothing came for her in her own name, which I find hard to accept for a home the two of us and our children live in.

I rang my bank on 15 April 2025 and the adviser looked up the transfer while I was on the line. She read out from her screen that the March rent of CHF 1,890 went out of my account on 27 March and carries 28 March as its value date, but that is only what she said to me over the telephone and I have not seen the account export myself.

Yesterday evening I went through the folder in our hallway cupboard and the termination on the official cantonal form from Hofmatt Immobilien AG came to light there. It is lying on the table in front of me and I can send it over as soon as you tell me where it should go.

What I would like checked is whether a termination that names only me can have any effect at all on a flat that is our family home, and whether it matters that the money had already left my account before the period they set had run out. Where I get stuck is the counting of that period: I do not know whether it started on the day the first letter was posted or on the day I collected it at the counter.

Before the present question can be answered, the execution date and the value date of the rent payment must stand established as attested by the bank. The evidence that carries this point is the bank's own export showing both dates for that transfer. What a party recounts about a record, whether from memory or from a telephone call with the institution, does not establish what the record says; the record itself, or an authenticated export of it, has to be on file.

It must also be established, ahead of the present decision, how the payment was booked and allocated on the manager's side. The property manager's ledger showing the posting of the amount and its allocation to the open items is the evidence for this. An account given by any party of what that ledger contains establishes nothing about its content; the ledger itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

The content and the service of the cure notice carrying the warning of termination, and of the termination given on the official form, must both be established before the decision is taken. Two routes are open: the cure notice as served, together with the official-form termination and the postal delivery proof for those notices; or, in their place, the authenticated chronology packet drawn from the landlord's system covering the notices and their service. A description or recollection of any of these documents by a party does not establish its content, so the document itself or the authenticated export is what has to be obtained.

An allocation statement for a mixed demand comes into play only where the property manager's ledger, once it has come back, actually reports a demand covering more than the rent. Until a return of that ledger reports such a circumstance, this obligation stays dormant, and for as long as it is dormant the property manager's ledger showing the posting and allocation of the payment is not to be requested.

The signed lease contract plays no part in this check and need not be obtained. Readiness here means no more than that the facts listed above stand established on the documents required for them; it settles nothing about legal entitlement.

Official cantonal form for the notification of the termination of a residential lease, dated 10 April 2025: Hofmatt Immobilien AG, Bahnhofstrasse 14, 8620 Wetzikon, gives notice to Daniel Zeller, Lindenweg 12, 8620 Wetzikon, terminating the lease over the three-and-a-half-room flat on the second floor as of 31 May 2025. The ground entered on the form is the non-payment of the rent for March 2025 of CHF 1,890.00 within the period set by the letter of 4 March 2025. The form is signed by V. Hofmatt for the landlord, its addressee field names Daniel Zeller alone, and it carries the standard note that the termination may be challenged before the conciliation authority within 30 days of receipt.

Authenticated extract from the correspondence register of Hofmatt Immobilien AG, generated and sealed by the system on 2 June 2025 for the object Lindenweg 12, 8620 Wetzikon. The entry of 4 March 2025 records the issue of the notice to remedy with warning of termination to Daniel Zeller, setting a period of 30 days for the March 2025 rent of CHF 1,890.00, dispatched by registered post the same day and collected on 6 March 2025; the entry of 10 April 2025 records the issue of the termination on the official form as of 31 May 2025 on the ground of non-payment, dispatched by registered post and signed for on 12 April 2025. The register holds no entry of any notice issued to Petra Zeller in respect of this object.
